title: The signature wait counts a proof as present only when its mirrored request carries the expected subject, so an old proof file never ends the wait
goal: Candidate 20e, G20-76 (observed live 2026-11-08 at the push of candidate 20d). `po-human-approval.mjs authorize-critical` mirrors request, proof, authority and signer into scratch/critical-<kind>-{request,proof,authority,signer}-<repo fingerprint>.json (criticalScratchArtifactPaths); the name is one fixed fingerprint per repository, so every signature of the same kind writes the SAME names (mirror order: request, proof, authority, signer, each overwritten in place). When an older mirror from an earlier signature still sits in scratch/, `proof-wait.mjs` (lib/signed-proof-wait.mjs observeProofFile) returns `proof-present` at once, because it only checks that a regular file with schema pipeline.po-approval-proof.v1 exists; `pipeline-state.mjs approve-push` then refuses with CRITICAL-PROOF-SUBJECT. Nothing is consumed, but the PO's signing round is wasted. Build, runner-neutral: (1) `awaitSignatureFields` (lib/signed-proof-wait.mjs) gains an optional `subjectSha256` (64 hex). When given, the returned waitAction argv carries a new flag `--subject <sha>` (add it to `proofWaitCommand` and to the closed flag set of `parse()` in scripts/proof-wait.mjs; a malformed value is PROOF-WAIT-ARGS), and `afterSigning` names that the wait ends only for the expected subject. (2) With a subject, `observeProofFile` reports `present` only when the proof file is well formed AND the sibling request (the existing `proof-` -> `request-` file-name mapping of `signCommandForProof`, same directory, scratch kind only) parses and carries exactly that subject, derived with the SAME function approve-push uses (criticalActionSubjectSha256 in lib/critical-action-approval-request.mjs), never a second spelling. A sibling request that is missing, unreadable, not JSON, of another schema or without a subject counts as `stale` (not signed yet): the wait keeps polling. Decide from the code whether the proof file itself also carries the subject and then check it too (the request is written before the proof, so a new request together with a proof file can still pair a new request with an OLD proof for a moment; the proof's own subject, when it has one, closes that window). Without a subject (a caller that does not know it) behaviour is byte-identical to today. A key-directory proof reference needs no change: its file name already contains the intent hash. (3) A timeout where a file existed but never matched ends with a NEW typed refusal code (for example PROOF-WAIT-STALE) whose single `repair` names the cause (an older signature's mirror sits at the path) and the exact recovery: move the scratch/critical-<kind>-* files aside (rename, never delete), have the PO run the one signing command again, then run the same wait; the existing PROOF-WAIT-TIMEOUT / PROOF-WAIT-INVALID texts stay. (4) Audit ALL four call sites of awaitSignatureFields and state per site in the notes whether a subject is available: scripts/push-prepare.mjs (subjectSha256 is already computed just above the call; pass it), scripts/pipeline-state.mjs (design approval), lib/project-onboarding-v3.mjs, lib/human-guard-override.mjs (key-directory form; expected unchanged). Pass the subject wherever the signing step has it and the proof is a scratch mirror; leave the others and say why. (5) docs: update the waitAction wording in docs/push-release-flow.md only if it describes the wait; add the interim hint to the notes (until installed, set old scratch/critical-* files aside before any push-prepare). Restate in place with a G20-76 comment any test that pins the old waitAction argv (QG-04: never weaken another assertion). Regression cases: a stale mirror (older request with another subject, or a request missing) does not end the wait and ends in the new code at timeout; the matching mirror ends it at once; no subject = old behaviour; push-prepare's report carries the subject in waitAction; the flag is parsed and a malformed subject is refused.
